faq.q: When is the best time to see the ice?
faq.a: From mid-February to mid-March. The ice is 60–100 cm thick, wind clears the snow and you can see the bottom in shallow bays.

faq.q: How do I get to Irkutsk?
faq.a: Direct flights from Moscow (6 h) and St Petersburg (6.5 h); connections via Moscow from most international hubs. Tours start with a pick-up at Irkutsk airport.
We only travel on checked ice roads using hovercraft and 4x4 vehicles with licensed drivers. If a section is unreliable, the route changes — this is written into every itinerary.
Most visitors need a Russian visa or an e-visa (available for 60+ countries). We provide the tour confirmation needed for the application.

chudesa-baykala.title: Wonders of Baikal
chudesa-baykala.tagline: Winter tour into the land of crystal ice
chudesa-baykala.summary: Five days for those who want action and ice sculptures up close: Listvyanka with dog sledding, an ice safari by hovercraft to Olkhon, Cape Khoboy by 4x4, Ogoy Island and a Buryat yurt lunch.
highlights: Hovercraft from Listvyanka to Olkhon via Peschanaya Bay and a natural ice rink
Cape Khoboy with fish soup cooked over a fire
Banya with a plunge pool on Olkhon
program: Airport pick-up. Taltsy open-air museum, dog sledding, cable car to Chersky Stone, Baikal Museum, fish market. Night in Listvyanka.
A full day on the ice by hovercraft: Peschanaya Bay, natural rink, methane bubbles. Evening arrival in Khuzhir.
4x4 to the island's northern tip through sacred sites. Fish soup by the fire. Banya in the evening.
Hovercraft across mirror ice to Ogoy, ice grottoes. Lunch in a Buryat yurt. Hotel in Irkutsk.
included: Entrance tickets and national park fees

City walk: wooden architecture, churches. Transfer.

dva-berega-baykala.tagline: Irkutsk ice and Buryat hot springs in one trip
dva-berega-baykala.summary: Seven days and both shores: Olkhon's ice hummocks in the west, Svyatoy Nos, Chivyrkuy Bay and hot springs in the east, ending at Ivolginsky Datsan near Ulan-Ude. We cross the lake on ice by hovercraft.

Thermal springs at Zmeinaya Bay and Goryachinsk
program: Taltsy, cable car, snowmobiles, Baikal Museum.
Hummocks, stilt trees of Peschanaya Bay, bubbles of Aya Bay, grottoes of Kobylya Golova.

Svyatoy Nos, Chivyrkuy Bay, ice cave, hot springs of Zmeinaya Bay.
Dog and reindeer sledding, Goryachinsk springs, Ivolginsky Datsan. Night in Ulan-Ude.

program: Airport pick-up, Taltsy, cable car, museum, lakeside walk. Night in Listvyanka.
